solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foul landing place for blow fly is here

definitions.meaning: an unfair or illegal action, especially an illegal punch in boxing
where a low punch lands, the illegal target area in boxing
the zipped opening on trousers sits just under the waistband

explanation.surface: A note about where a blowfly lands, oddly called foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow fly' reads as one insect but splits across two definitions: a punch's landing place, and the trouser fly's position. Three definitions in one clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing idiom for an illegal low punch is used generally for any unfair remark or tactic.

clue.text: Flipping bed clothes don't wear out

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so the bed's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
to last is to endure without wearing out

explanation.surface: Turning the bedclothes so they don't wear out too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like turning the bed over; it is the mild oath. 'clothes' is a verb here, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British curses used as intensifiers, like 'damned' or 'wretched'.

clue.text: Untruth about dealing with one's honour

indicators.note: the lie's letters are placed about, that is around, the next pieces

parts.note: an untruth is a lie
a talk on a topic deals with it, so on means dealing with
one's contracts to 'I is', with I as the numeral one

explanation.surface: A falsehood concerning how a person's honour was handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I plus S, read as I'S with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone as a celebrity is to honour and fete them.

clue.text: Quickly — what is the anagram?

indicators.note: the clue openly asks for a rearrangement of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Someone impatiently demanding the solution to a puzzle, fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names its own device: the anagram of WHAT IS THE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something speedily, with hurry, is doing it rapidly.

clue.text: So upset about love cheat

indicators.note: the turned word goes about, round, the next piece
in a down clue an upset word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: so and such are interchangeable intensifiers: 'so good', 'such good'
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone so upset about being cheated on in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SUCH to HCUS; 'about' then wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick or hoax someone, as in hocus-pocus, is to swindle them.

clue.text: Dress in black and appear older

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to age is to grow or look older

explanation.surface: Wearing black clothes adds years to one's appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is a verb or a garment on the surface; here it is a wound dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing for a wound is a strip of gauze or cloth wrapped round it.

clue.text: With more fat I will have buttery coating

indicators.note: the pantry word coats, covers round, the single letter

parts.note: a buttery is a store room for provisions, like a larder

explanation.surface: A cook adding a buttery coating to make food richer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttery' looks like an adjective about butter; it is the noun, an old word for a pantry, as in college butteries.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of an adjective meaning fatty or greasy, like pork fat.

clue.text: Mushrooms and battered tripe for sale

indicators.note: battered means beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A food stall offering mushrooms and battered tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushrooms' looks like a noun on a menu; it is the verb, to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that mushrooms spreads or multiplies quickly, growing in number.

clue.text: Show 'choose' as 'choose again'

parts.note: a meter reads a value when it shows it
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction to display one word as a fuller phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show ... as' sounds like a typesetting instruction; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up again something chosen earlier, such as a policy, is re-selecting it.

clue.text: Will not split (Scottish spelling)

parts.note: will not becomes 'can't', both refusals
a rip is a split or tear

explanation.surface: A refusal to split up, with a note that the word is spelt the Scottish way.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a dictionary note on spelling; 'spelling' means casting a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a witch's charm or magic trick, so a piece of Scottish spell-casting.

clue.text: Simple Plan covering single, one by Rod Stewart

indicators.note: the plan's letters cover, go round, the single letter

parts.note: taken as written; the band Simple Plan is suggested by the surface
single is one, the Roman numeral I
Sailing was a 1975 number one single for Rod Stewart

explanation.surface: The band Simple Plan doing a cover of a Rod Stewart single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple Plan' reads as a band name; it splits into the definition and the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy progress with no difficulties, a figurative phrase from smooth navigation.

clue.text: Check this bad language

parts.note: a let is a check or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the word's letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: A warning to watch someone's swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad language' reads as swearing; 'bad' is the anagram signal and 'language' alone defines. 'bad' makes TISH from THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an old name for Latvian, the Baltic tongue spoken in Latvia.

clue.text: Cuckoo tangles flipping legs

indicators.note: flipping turns the combined pieces over so they are read backwards

parts.note: the ani is a black American bird of the cuckoo family
mats are tangled masses of hair or fibre

explanation.surface: A crazy person getting legs tangled while doing flips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like an adjective, mad; it is the bird. 'flipping' turns ANIMATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or runner that 'has legs' has the endurance to keep going.

clue.text: Sweet stall

definitions.meaning: a soft confection of sugar, butter and milk
to stall is to evade or delay by being vague

explanation.surface: A sweet stall at a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft toffee-like confection; also to dodge or blur an issue to put off deciding.

clue.text: Ancient court and shrine in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Archaeologists describing an old courthouse and temple lying ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme council and tribunal of the Jews in ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Disgraceful American supports recent Olympic ban?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a ban on the 2016 Games could be put as 'no to Rio'
US stands for American, as in the US of A

explanation.surface: A US citizen backing a shameful ban on a recent Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a made-up phrase: NO TO RIO, a veto on the Rio de Janeiro Olympics of 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Well known for something bad, infamous, so scandalous in reputation.

clue.text: Mean salesman's grudge

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative; the 's links him to the next piece
to grudge is to resent

explanation.surface: A stingy sales rep nursing a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy; it is the verb, to signify.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for or signify something, as a symbol stands for an idea.

clue.text: This can be spread all over bone

parts.note: pate, a meat or fish paste, is spread on toast

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, the word read upwards

explanation.surface: A spread you can slather over a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This can be spread' is a cryptic pointer to a spread, not a definition of the answer. 'over' turns ALL into LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap, the small flat bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Old enough to be a model

parts.note: ex- means former, old
ample means enough or more

explanation.surface: Someone now old enough to become a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk job; it is a pattern or specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern to follow or an instance that illustrates a type.

clue.text: Good group in cricket ground

parts.note: Abba is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A decent band playing at a cricket stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gabba is the main cricket ground in Brisbane, Australia, used for Test matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for Brisbane's Woolloongabba stadium, a Test match venue.

clue.text: Country houses like rough monthly charge?

indicators.note: Great Britain houses, holds inside, the comparison word

parts.note: GB is the abbreviation for the country Great Britain
as means like, as in 'white as snow'
feeling rough is feeling ill

explanation.surface: Big country houses feel the pinch of rough monthly bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country houses' looks like stately homes; 'houses' is the containment verb. The question mark allows that these are often quarterly.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular statement for domestic fuel supply, an example of a recurring household charge.

clue.text: Gathering family to find direct route

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for work or fun, as in a sewing bee
a line is a family lineage

explanation.surface: A family reunion where everyone takes the most direct way there.
explanation.definitionFit: The straight path a bee is supposed to fly home, so the shortest way.

clue.text: One flying boat on right, unfinished

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a title is a legal right to property
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A lone pilot flying a boat with the right of way, journey unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit, a small songbird, so something that flies.

clue.text: Grasp the same wooden fencing?

parts.note: ken is understanding, grasp, as in 'beyond my ken'
do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Grabbing the same fence of wooden palings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wooden fencing' looks like a garden fence; it is swordplay with wooden or bamboo swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese martial art of sword fighting with bamboo staves, so fencing with wood.

clue.text: Rumours of sightings all started right here

definitions.text: Rumours of sightings all started right here

indicators.note: the beginning of each of those words is taken

parts.note: well and right both mean fine or in good order, as in 'all is well'

explanation.surface: The town where tales of UFO sightings began.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the 1947 UFO crash claims in New Mexico started there.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Mexico town at the heart of the 1947 flying-saucer stories and alien legends.

clue.text: Part of desert area covered in exotic plants

indicators.note: the area letter is covered, enclosed, by the rearranged plants
exotic means foreign and strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patch of desert overgrown with foreign plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' makes SALTPN, and 'covered in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry basin where evaporated water leaves a crust of salt, found in deserts.

clue.text: View over wing

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A view seen over a wing, from an aeroplane seat.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or judgement someone holds.

clue.text: Male model is going out with English girl

indicators.note: with joins the next piece on after the rearranged letters
going out suggests leaving the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A male model dating an English girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like dating; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: French title for an unmarried young woman, so a young lady or miss.
